Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get your schedule on the day orientation day, which resulted in several overlapping courses for me. But the first 1,5 week you can attend all the classes you are thinking about and then decide which to finally enroll in

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student information system of the university and the Erasmus office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of my courses overlapped, so some things changed, but in the end i was satisfied with my courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time and try out the classes before deciding

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level at Charles University seemed lower than what I am used to in University of Copenhagen

questions.answer: UCPH is way better structured than Charles University

Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's a very good free opportunity to do sports at the University if you are prepared to go to the a different faculty (I think it was somewhere in Prague 10)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus Club of the Science Faculty offered different events and trips to get to know czech culture and other Erasmus students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visit the some of all the beautiful nature and historical cities outside of Prague

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of Prague. It's really cheap to travel by train when you get your International student identity card

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the locals are usually nice and helpful (if they speak english)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Prague is in general a very nice city and their love and passion for good coffee and beer is worth appreciating

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you're in the Science Faculty: Go on the trips they host, it's a nice way to meet people across the science studies
Use the first week to attend different courses before you decide which you will enroll in
Have fun and don't stress to much about it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over Europe and learning about their cultures

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Saying goodbye to all the amazing people I meet throughout the 5 months I spent in Prague

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
